evidence_wording:
May be more likely than SSRIs to improve social and work
functioning
Side effects may appear “anticholinergic,” but reboxetine does not
directly block muscarinic receptors
Thus, antidotes for these side effects can be alpha 1 antagonists
such as tamsulosin, especially for urinary retention in men over 50
with borderline urine flow
Cognitive disturbance
Psychomotor retardation
May be effective if SSRIs have failed or for SSRI “poop-out”
Reboxetine is a mixture of an active and an inactive enantiomer, and
the active enantiomer may be developed in future clinical testing
Constipation, dry mouth, and urinary retention are noradrenergic,
due in part to peripheral alpha 1 receptor stimulation causing
decreased acetylcholine release
Novel use of reboxetine may be for attention deficit disorder,
analogous to the actions of another norepinephrine selective
reuptake inhibitor, atomoxetine, but few controlled studies
Another novel use may be for neuropathic pain, alone or in
combination with other antidepressants, but few controlled studies
Some studies suggest efficacy in panic disorder
